title: Rav Nachman bar Oshpazti (Oshparti)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Taanit 24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.24b.10) relates that Rav Papa decreed a fast. Feeling faint, he tasted something and swallowed a bowlful of porridge. He prayed for rain, but none came. Rav Nachman bar Oshpazti joked: “If the Master swallows another bowlful, rain will come.”
The Arukh, under bar, says this is Rav Papa’s mother’s name and reads bar Oshparti. Hyman concludes: “We must say that he is R’ Nachman bar Yitzchak.”[^4]

notes.text: The Arukh’s statement concerns Rav Papa’s mother according to Hyman, whereas the entry concerns Rav Nachman; the referent and Hyman’s concluding identification remain unresolved. “Slurped” corrects the earlier “burned.”

The saved whole Lublin1883 Arukh Letter Bet346 scalar explicitly gives bar Oshparti and says it is Rav Papa’s mother’s name. This confirms that reported wording without establishing how to punctuate Nachman’s address or that Nachman must be bar Yitzchak. Hyman’s WE MUST SAY force is preserved under attribution, not accepted genealogy. Oshpazti/Oshparti remain alternatives. Slurping is retained rather than the older burned-bowl translation; no fresh Taanit paragraph was supplied. Full Rav for the locally repeated Nachman is grounded in the heading; the concluding different bar-Yitzchak identification stays R’.

In the consulted Taanit 24b, the speaker is called “Rav Nachman bar Oshpazti,” and the verb describes swallowing the porridge. The story ends with Rav Papa’s embarrassment and the arrival of rain. Hyman gives an abridged account. The Arukh, Letter Bet 346, gives Oshparti and calls it Rav Papa’s mother’s name. Seder HaDorot 2695 also records competing readings and different ways to understand the name. Hyman’s conclusion about Nachman bar Yitzchak is his own identification.

[Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2695&lang=en) discusses the Arukh’s interpretation, the Yuchasin’s reading of the patronymic, and the alternative name he reports from Ein Yaakov. Hyman gives his own identification in the last sentence.
